data.title: BCE explores potential Telus deal as Quebecor's C$31B proposal faces scrutiny - report
data.description:
BCE (BCE), the parent company of Bell Canada, held preliminary discussions with Telus (TU) and hired financial and legal advisers as it explores a potential transaction with the telecommunications company following Quebecor's (QBCRF) C$31B takeover proposal, The Globe and Mail reported Thursday, citing three people familiar with the matter.

The discussions are at an early stage, and one source said BCE (BCE) would also need to consider what concessions or regulatory remedies the Canadian government might require to approve a potential deal, according to the report.

Quebecor (QBCRF) made its C$31B proposal public on November 16, offering Telus (TU) shareholders C$6.35 in cash and 0.17 of a Quebecor (QBCRF) Class B share for each Telus (TU) share. The consideration values Telus (TU) at ~C$19.45 per share, representing a premium of about 60% to its November 13 closing price.

Under the proposed transaction, Telus (TU) shareholders would receive ~54% of the combined company's economic interest but only about 23% of its voting rights. Quebecor's (QBCRF) controlling shareholder, the Péladeau family, would retain voting control.

Quebecor (QBCRF) estimates the combination would generate C$160M in annual operating synergies and C$235M in annual capital efficiencies.

Telus (TU) has formed a special committee to review the proposal and explore strategic alternatives. The company has questioned the offer's valuation, governance structure, regulatory prospects, and projected leverage.

data.title: Citigroup CEO Fraser warns of more tech outages as firms patch tech
data.description:
• Citigroup (C) CEO Jane Fraser cautioned that tech outages risk becoming more routine as companies race to patch their systems and tighten security.
  • “The volume of changes — the patches — that is going through the world’s tech stack at the same time is five- to 10-fold what we’ve ever seen before,” Fraser said at a Bloomberg Newsmakers event Wednesday.
  • “We should be expecting for a while some more downtime, some more outages in different areas.” Fraser said she is not surprised by recent tech outages across the US. 
  • Large U.S. bank stock prices neared the rare 'death cross' bearish technical chart pattern recently, with the KBW Bank Index's (BKX) 50-day moving average almost falling below its 200-day moving average. The index was down as much as 2.4% on Nov. 17, a day after JPMorgan Chase (JPM) faced a "technical issue" that had caused customers' transactions to take longer to process on Monday. Other bank stocks, such as Bank of America (BAC), US Bank (USB), and Wells Fargo (WFC), were also impacted.

data.title: Intel lands first external customer for 18A-P chips
data.description:
Intel (INTC) CEO Lip-Bu Tan said on Wednesday that the company has signed the first outside customer for its 18A chips. INTC shares rose 2.6% in extended trading. 

“Resilient supply on the foundry is very important,” Tan said at the TomorrowX Summit in Austin, Texas, according to CNBC. “And then 18A, I’m involved in production and we just signed the first customer,” Tan added, without naming the debut client.

It’s a milestone moment for Intel in its five-year effort to take on chip manufacturing leader Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSM). “It’s a huge win for foundry,” Creative Strategies analyst Ben Bajarin told CNBC in an interview.

Pushkar Ranade, Intel’s technology chief, clarified on X that the external customer had signed up for Intel’s 18A-P manufacturing process node, which went into risk production in June. In May, reports indicated that Apple (AAPL) and Intel (INTC) were closing in on a deal to use Intel’s foundry to make some of the chips for Apple devices.

Earlier this month Intel (INTC) shareholders sued the company for allegedly misleading investors about the impact that a slowdown in personal ​computer sales had on its Q3 results, which caused its stock to plunge nearly 29% in a single day.

data.title: Musk: Jensen Huang irreplaceable, regrets midterm spend
data.description:
Tesla (TSLA) and SpaceX (SPCX) CEO Elon Musk likened Jensen Huang’s departure from Nvidia (NVDA) to kicking Michael Jordan off a team riding a winning streak, while expressing regret over how much he spent on the U.S. midterm elections.

“You’ve got a winning streak ... and then you kick Michael Jordan off your team,” Musk told during an interview at The New York Times’ DealBook Summit on Wednesday. He added, “Doesn’t seem like a smart decision to me.”

The SpaceX and Tesla chief executive, who previously said it would be an “honor” to hire the Nvidia co-founder, added that no one could really replace Huang. Musk said he had heard similar views about Huang’s departure from Nvidia, including from President Donald Trump.

“I think the president has voiced publicly that he thinks Jensen should have stayed as CEO, and everyone I know thinks the same ... this is, at the end of the day, the Nvidia board decision,” he said, adding, “We’re not on the board, right?”

Tesla has been one of Nvidia’s key customers, while Huang has frequently commended Musk’s AI ambitions, particularly Tesla’s autonomous driving technology, xAI, and its Optimus humanoid robot.

Asked about the midterms, Musk said he felt “pretty foolish” about spending at least $474M with little to show for it, though he added that “maybe it would have been much worse without that,” according to a CNBC report.

Musk said his goal had been to prevent the presidency, House, and Senate from all being controlled by one party. “If I could rewind the clock, I would have spent less money,” he added.

data.title: British Land Company Non-GAAP EPS of 16.10p, net rental income of £264M; upgrades FY27 underlying EPS guidance
Thursday’s Economic Calendar
data.description:
8:30 AM Jobless Claims

New unemployment claims are compiled weekly to show the number of individuals who filed for unemployment insurance for the first time.

Claims are expected to go back down to 198K after rising 9K to 200K last week.

8:30 AM Philadelphia Fed Manufacturing Index

The general conditions index from this business outlook survey is a diffusion index of manufacturing conditions within the Philadelphia Federal Reserve district. 

Business expansion expected to improve to an index of 23.2 in November from 20.9 in October.

8:50 AM Beth Hammack Speaks

Gives opening remarks before the 14th annual Financial Stability Conference hosted by the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland and the Yale Program on Financial Stability.

9:25 AM Philip Jefferson Speaks

Participates virtually in the "Economic Shocks" panel before the International Monetary Fund and Central Bank of Brazil conference, "A Quarter Century of Inflation Targeting in Latin America: Progress, Challenges, and the Road Ahead"

10:00 AM E-Commerce Retail Sales 

E-commerce sales are sales of goods and services where an order is placed by the buyer or where price and terms of sale are negotiated over the Internet, an extranet, Electronic Data Interchange network, or another online system.

10:00 AM Leading Indicators

The index of leading economic indicators is a composite of 10 forward-looking components, including building permits, new factory orders, and unemployment claims.

The leading index is expected to be flat for a second straight month.

10:30 AM EIA Natural Gas Report

The Energy Information Administration  provides weekly information on natural gas stocks in underground storage for the U.S. and five regions of the country. 

11:00 AM Kansas City Fed Manufacturing Index

The Kansas City Fed index offers a monthly assessment of change in the region's manufacturing sector. 

12:30 PM Austan Goolsbee Speaks

Participates in moderated Q&A before an Economic Club of Indiana Speaker Series luncheon.

1:00 PM 10-Yr TIPS Auction

The Treasury sells Treasury Inflation-Protected Securities, also known as TIPS, at regularly scheduled auctions. 

2:15 PM Michael Barr Speaks

Speaks on artificial intelligence before the FinRegLab 2026 AI Symposium.

4:00 PM Thomas Barkin Speaks

Participates in fireside chat on the economy before the Virginia Senate Finance Appropriations Committee Annual Meeting.

4:30 PM Fed Balance Sheet

The Fed's balance sheet is a weekly report presenting a consolidated balance sheet for all 12 Reserve Banks that lists factors supplying reserves into the banking system and factors absorbing reserves from the system.

6:30 PM Anna Paulson Speaks

Speaks on "Communications and Monetary Policy" before the Money Marketeers of New York University.
